rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation affects the return statement at line 200 inside `if (return_indices)` block. With default `return_indices=False`, this block never executes. The 112 test rounds passed bitwise-equivalent because the mutated code path was never triggered. Changing `return_indices` to `True` requires model reconfiguration, not input value changes.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutant survives because the mutation is located in code that only executes when the model's `return_indices` parameter is set to `True`. The default value is `False`, and the testing framework only allows varying input tensor values, not model configuration parameters. The `generate_inputs(device)` function cannot change how the model was instantiated. When `return_indices=False`, the entire `if (return_indices)` block is skipped, so the mutated `torch::cat` call is never reached regardless of what input values are provided.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed testing contract. To kill it, one would need to instantiate the model with `return_indices=True`, which would cause a shape mismatch error (concatenating tensors of shapes [B,C,L,1] and [B,C,L]). However, changing model configuration is outside the scope of allowed test modifications.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should consider model configuration parameters as part of the testing contract. When mutations affect code paths controlled by configuration flags, tests should be generated that exercise all reachable configurations. Additionally, the EMD pipeline could detect that the mutation is in a conditional block and verify whether that condition is ever true in the test configuration.
